clue.text: Large bills for mail-order customers?

definitions.meaning: bills stuck up on walls and hoardings to advertise something
whimsically, people who post off their orders

explanation.surface: A remark about the hefty invoices sent to people who shop by mail order.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, invented sense: people who send things through the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Placards pasted up as advertisements are bills, and anyone sending a letter by mail is literally one who posts.

clue.text: Carefully read through, then utilised

parts.note: per means through or by way of, as in per post
used means utilised

explanation.surface: Someone studied a document closely and then put it to use.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse is to study or examine a text in detail.

clue.text: Really good drink offered with little hesitation

parts.note: to sup is to drink, or a sup is a mouthful
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A fine drink handed over after a brief pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is informal praise meaning excellent.

clue.text: A bore keen to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard means the word for keen is spoken and a soundalike is written

parts.note: eager means keen

explanation.surface: A tedious person who is desperate for attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' suggests a tedious person, but it is a tidal wave surging up a river; the eagre is the one on England's River Trent.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal surge running up a narrowing estuary is called a bore, and the Trent's is known by this name.

clue.text: Point to a mad character responsible for smash

parts.note: S is south, a point of the compass
the Mad Hatter is a character in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland

explanation.surface: Blaming a crazy figure for a breakage.
explanation.definitionFit: To break something into pieces is to smash it.

clue.text: A contrivance of the scholar with backbone

parts.note: an MA, a Master of Arts, is a stock crossword scholar
a chine is an animal's spine, or a cut of meat along it

explanation.surface: Describing a gadget invented by a determined academic with plenty of spine.
explanation.definitionFit: A device or apparatus built to do a job is a contrivance.

clue.text: Name the new fuel

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so these letters are made into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to give a recently invented fuel its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is the chief component of natural gas, burnt for energy.

clue.text: A dance where lots of tea will be provided

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea, and lots of it means several servings
cha again, a second serving of the slang word for tea
cha once more, a third serving of the slang word for tea

explanation.surface: A ballroom event where plenty of tea is served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots of' asks for several helpings of the slang word for tea, here three in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha-cha is a lively Latin American ballroom routine.

clue.text: Stimulating and popular single, well-housed

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: housed means the single letter is lodged within the word for well

parts.note: a spring is a natural well or source of water
I is the Roman numeral for one, a single

explanation.surface: A hit record that is lively and comes from a well-to-do home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' suggests a record, but it gives I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rouses or motivates people is stimulating.

clue.text: Call in the president — it lends authority

indicators.note: in signals that the letters lie hidden inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Summon the head of state, as their presence gives weight to proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Authority' also hints at the answer's sense of giving someone a right.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a title or name is to call them something.

clue.text: Giving a grunt, pen letters, finding it distasteful

indicators.note: giving in the sense of bending or yielding, so these letters lose their shape and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone grunting while writing letters finds the whole business unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving' signals the anagram of A GRUNT and PEN; 'letters' and 'finding it' are only link words in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something offensive or loathsome is distasteful.

clue.text: A fool, and in Paris that's an advantage

parts.note: an ass is a fool
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: Being a fool turns out to be useful when you are in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A useful quality or valuable possession counts as an advantage.

clue.text: Present dreadful crawler

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something mangled or done badly, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A gift turns out to be a horrible creeping creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake moves along the ground on its belly, so it is a crawler.

clue.text: A non-drinker, he is at heart a sceptic

indicators.note: at heart means the words he is sit in the middle of the abstainer's letters

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, someone who abstains from alcohol
taken as written

explanation.surface: Describing a man who doesn't drink and, deep down, doubts everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who denies the existence of God is a religious sceptic.

clue.text: Underworld instruction to settle accounts

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
a charge is a formal instruction, as a judge gives to a jury

explanation.surface: A gangster's order to pay off what is owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld' suggests gangsters, but it is the classical realm of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay off a debt in full is to settle accounts, as in discharging an obligation.

clue.text: Personal subscription

parts.note: subscription in its literal sense, something written underneath, done in one's own hand

explanation.definitionFit: Literally a subscription is writing below a document, and one's own name written there is how you sign it.

clue.text: Dicky hid things, showing belated wisdom

indicators.note: dicky means shaky or unsound, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who concealed items shows understanding too late.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindsight is understanding of events only after they have happened.

clue.text: Agree to strike

definitions.meaning: to fit in or harmonise, as opinions that ... with each other
what a clock or bell does when it sounds the hour

explanation.definitionFit: Ideas that harmonise are said to chime, and a clock ringing out the hour strikes.

clue.text: Gas — nitrogen — loaded onto an old ship

indicators.note: loaded onto means the symbol is put on board, following the ship's name

parts.note: the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Cargo of a gas being put aboard an ancient vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is an inert element, one of the noble gases.

clue.text: Boldly confronts a number over expenses

indicators.note: over means the first letters sit above the expenses in this down entry

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number
costs are expenses

explanation.surface: Someone challenges a figure written above the expense claims.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and address them aggressively.

clue.text: Figure about a hundred get confused

parts.note: re means about or concerning
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to tangle is to get muddled or knotted

explanation.surface: A diagram of roughly a hundred things all in a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-sided shape with right angles is a geometric figure.

clue.text: A stock-taker making little sound?

definitions.meaning: someone who takes livestock, a cattle thief
one who rustles, making soft crackling noises

explanation.definitionFit: A cattle thief steals livestock, and something that rustles makes a faint crackle.

clue.text: The case for getting top politicians together

definitions.meaning: a cupboard or display case with shelves or drawers
the senior ministers of a government as a body

explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard for storing things, and the group of senior government ministers.

clue.text: Intent on eastern development

indicators.note: development suggests something changing form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone keen on growth in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Being serious and determined about something is being intent.

clue.text: Categorises as cold girls

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Someone sorting young women as frosty.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort things into groups or types is to categorise them.

clue.text: Bound to take in a paying guest

indicators.note: to take in means the boundary word swallows the letter a

parts.note: a bound is a boundary or border

explanation.surface: Someone obliged to accommodate a lodger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'obliged to', but 'Bound' is a noun meaning a limit.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodger who pays for room and meals is a paying guest.

clue.text: A deliberate lighting offence

parts.note: the crime of setting fire to property on purpose

explanation.definitionFit: The criminal act of setting fire to property on purpose.

clue.text: Duck when the dunderhead playboy appears!

parts.note: the head of the word dunder is its first letter, D
a rake is a dissolute playboy

explanation.surface: Take cover when a fool of a womaniser turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dunderhead' reads as a fool, but split as dunder-head it gives the first letter of dunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The male of the mallard and other waterfowl has its own name, as a cockerel does among hens.

clue.text: Beasts holding a trainee back will be suspended

indicators.note: back means the whole assembly is read in reverse
holding means the animals' letters enclose the learner

parts.note: gnus, or wildebeest, are African beasts
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Animals carrying a learner on their backs will be strung up.
explanation.walkthrough: GNUS holding L gives GNULS, which 'back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hung up or dangling from a support has been slung.

clue.text: A painting of a head of state?

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as a ..., a headland belonging to a country

explanation.surface: Asking whether a portrait shows a president or monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of state' suggests a ruler, but a cape is a headland, so a state's head is a land's cape.
explanation.definitionFit: A view of rural scenery is a type of picture, and a cape is a promontory of a country.

clue.text: Scatter these around left and right for protection

indicators.note: scatter tells you to throw these letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to throw things about on both sides as a defensive measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scatter' mixes THESE, which goes 'around' L and R in the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere offering cover from weather or danger gives protection.

clue.text: Brown, a little gentleman, won't cross the line

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun: the geometric line that touches a curve without crossing it

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
gent is a shortened form of gentleman

explanation.surface: A man named Brown, a small polite fellow, refuses to break the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a surname, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry such a line meets a curve at one point and touches it without cutting through.
